description: From **1861** to **1865**, the United States is torn apart: more than **620,000** dead. At the heart of the conflict, slavery, national unity, and the birth of a stronger federal state.

hero.hook: The deadliest war in American history, for the Union and against slavery.

blocks.text: From **1861** to **1865**, the United States experiences its most serious crisis: the Civil War. The North (the Union) versus the South (the Confederacy). No more **620,000** dead.
The conflict transforms a young republic into an industrial power, at the cost of lasting trauma to national unity and slavery.
The **North** is industrializing, with wages and protectionism. The **South** remains rural, rich in cotton produced by **4 million** slaves.

blocks.caption: Southern Plantation: Slavery at the Heart of the Confederate Economy.

blocks.text: The debate also concerns the **[[States' rights vs. the federal government]]**: who decides on slavery, the local state or Washington? The election of **Abraham Lincoln** (**November 1860**), Republican opposed to the extension of slavery, without a single vote from the South, triggers secession. Seven states found the Confederacy, with as president, and guaranteed slavery in their constitutions. **[[Jefferson Davis]]**
Before the war, we often said “the United States *is*” in the plural. Afterwards, the use of the singular (“*East*”) is essential: an indivisible nation.

**April 12, 1861**, Southern cannons bombard Fort Sumter, South Carolina. The war, which we thought would be short, became industrial. In **Antietam** (**September 17, 1862**), **23,000** victims in twelve hours: the bloodiest day in American military history.

The failure of , the main Confederate general, allowed Lincoln to sign  (**January 1, 1863**), which freed slaves in the rebel states. The war for the Union also became a war for freedom, which closed the door to European support for the South. **Gettysburg** (July **1863**) breaks the Confederate momentum. **[[Robert E. Lee]]** **[[The Emancipation Proclamation (January 1st, 1863)]]**

blocks.caption: Battle of the Civil War: unprecedented industrial violence.

blocks.text: , Union general-in-chief, is waging a war of attrition. His lieutenant **William Tecumseh Sherman** ravaged Georgia during his “March to the Sea”. Lee surrendered at **Appomattox** on **April 9, 1865**. **[[Ulysses Grant]]**

blocks.caption: Abraham Lincoln, President of the Union, assassinated five days after Appomattox.

blocks.text: Five days later, Lincoln was assassinated by **John Wilkes Booth**, a southern actor. The **[[Reconstruction (1865-1877)]]**, period of reconstruction of the South, begins without him. In December **1865**, abolished slavery nationwide. [[The 13th Amendment]]
The war also accelerated surgery: doctors like **Gurdon Buck** carried out the first facial reconstructions on soldiers disfigured by Minié bullets.

Under the **[[Reconstruction (1865-1877)]]** (**1865-1877**), African Americans voted and were elected. Then comes the reaction: the **[[Ku Klux Klan]]** (**1865**), white terrorist organization, the withdrawal of federal troops (**1877**), Jim Crow segregation laws. Legal segregation would last nearly a century.
On the map, a united nation without legal slavery. In fact, a deep racial divide. And the tools of a future world power: heavy industry, railways, a strong federal state.

events.detail: End of fighting and constitutional abolition.
events.title: Appomattox and 13th Amendment

blocks.text: The Civil War (**1861-1865**) unified the United States and abolished slavery, at the cost of **620,000** deaths, while leaving a racial divide that Jim Crow laws would prolong.
